text: The NYSC was established by Decree No. 24 of 22 May 1973, after the Nigerian Civil War, to develop common ties among Nigerian youths and promote national unity.
The objectives of the NYSC scheme are set out in Decree No. 51 of 16 June 1993, and include instilling discipline, industry, and patriotic service in Nigerian youths.
The Director-General of the NYSC is Brigadier General Olakunle Oluseye Nafiu.
The NYSC Directorate Headquarters is at Plot 416, Tigris Crescent, Off Aguiyi Ironsi Street, Maitama, Abuja. General enquiries: info@nysc.gov.ng.

The number to call in an emergency is the NYSC's 24/7 Distress Call Centre emergency short code, 6972, reachable from any Nigerian mobile network. Corps members and the public can dial this number in an emergency to reach NYSC directly.
The only official NYSC websites are nysc.gov.ng, nysc.org.ng, and the registration portal portal.nysc.org.ng. Prospective corps members register online at portal.nysc.org.ng.

The NYSC service year has four segments, and a corps member must satisfactorily complete all four to earn the certificate of national service: the orientation course, primary assignment, Community Development Service (CDS), and winding-up/passing-out.
The service year begins with a compulsory orientation course held in camp, lasting three weeks, for all graduates mobilised for national service.
The orientation course opens with a swearing-in ceremony presided over by the State Governor (or FCT Minister), with the oath of allegiance administered by the state's Chief Judge.

Orientation camp activities include physical training and drills, lectures on the host state's people and culture, professional lectures, skill acquisition (SAED) training, Man O' War drills, and social competitions such as football, volleyball, cooking, dance and drama.

After orientation camp, corps members are posted to their Place of Primary Assignment (PPA). Postings consider a member's specialization, with emphasis on rural postings in agriculture, health, education and infrastructure. Corps members are expected to accept their posting.

Community Development Service (CDS) is the segment of the service year where corps members identify the needs of their host communities and mobilise residents to carry out projects, such as classrooms, health centres, literacy campaigns and sensitization programmes.

Winding-up/passing-out happens around the 12th month of service. Corps members submit final clearance letters from their employers, attend debriefing, and participate in the passing-out ceremony, where outstanding members may receive a State Honours Award.

To register, prospective corps members need a functional email address and a Nigerian (GSM) phone number. The email and password are used to log in to the NYSC portal afterwards, so they should be kept safe.

Locally trained graduates must register with their correct matriculation number, and only those whose names appear on the Senate/Academic Board Approved Result list submitted by their institution can register on the NYSC portal.
Anyone who presents fake documents during NYSC registration will be demobilised, decamped, and handed over to law enforcement for prosecution.
Registration passport photographs must show the face fully (eyes, nose, ears, mouth, jaw), fill and be centred in the frame, and have a white or off-white background with no shadow.

Registration by proxy is prohibited. Prospective corps members should remember which fingers they used for biometric capture, because the same fingers are used for verification at orientation camp — anyone who cannot be verified will not be registered in camp.

Paying the optional fee of N2,786.24 lets a prospective corps member receive their call-up number by SMS and print their call-up letter online. Those who don't pay can collect their call-up number and letter from their institution instead. Anyone who paid previously but wasn't mobilised does not pay again.
The orientation camp is not suitable for pregnant women and nursing mothers, and NYSC states they will not be accommodated in camp.
Part-time graduates do not serve; they register online and print an exclusion letter from the portal.
Foreign-trained graduates have separate mobilization requirements (published on the NYSC site) and must use Nigerian phone numbers during online registration.

NYSC publishes mobilization support phone lines by geo-political zone: South East 08092142614, South South 08102790538, North Central 08092142661, South West 09038034460, North West 08092142616, North East 07018836388.

The federal NYSC allowance is N77,000 per month (national minimum wage of N70,000 plus 10%), paid equally to all corps members nationwide since March 2025, usually between the 25th and 30th of each month.

Some state governments pay corps members an extra monthly allowance on top of the federal N77,000. State allowances are optional, vary by state and PPA type, and can change or stop without notice, so they should be treated as a bonus rather than guaranteed income.
Allawee is Nigerian slang for the monthly NYSC allowance corps members are paid.
The government allowance is another name for the NYSC allowance, since it is paid by the federal government (and, in some states, an extra amount by the state government too).

text: Corps members are covered under NHIA (National Health Insurance Authority) enrolment; details are on the NYSC website's NHIA Enrolment page.
Relocation after camp is available to a corps member with a genuine reason (such as marriage, health, or security), who can apply through the NYSC portal to move to another state.
